description: Follow-up of skills-f49 (2026-09-23). title: A reading of field evidence became the frame of the work without its edges being read
description:
In a real run (meshynet, P0 outage). At the preflight the agent read a field capture and told the owner the sharpest fact in the whole record: the relay re-dialled the exit node every 45 seconds, had been doing so for hours before the policy publication, and the cycle broke off exactly at the head change — therefore the publication did not so much break the network as stop the mechanism that had been patching it. On that reading the agent reframed the P0, opened a task, and wrote a change record that the owner approved and that was merged into master.

Three hours later a worker checked the journal and contradicted it. The agent re-read it itself: the period of 45 seconds was real, but all 34 dials fit into 25 minutes and ended with a daemon restart 4h25m before the publication. 'For hours' and 'broke off at the head change' were never in the evidence: the agent had seen a run of consecutive lines and never looked at the first, the last or the count. The false fact sat in an approved record in master and in the task, and the conclusion built on it — the link between that defect and the outage — was wrong.

The protocol says a design decision comes with the measurement that shows what fails, but nothing says what a reading of a log or a capture must carry before it is stated as a fact. Duration and coincidence in time are exactly the two claims a sample never contains.
close_reason: fixed in 25710ca

title: A run's forecast was answered by the calendar, and its measured hours were hidden behind a verdict
description:
Found in real use on 2026-09-22, looking at seven recorded runs across two projects.

What happened. The run journal compared a forecast to the wall clock between start and finish, so a run forecast at 240 minutes was recorded as having taken 2889: the nights the owner was away sat inside the number, and the ratio it produced was noise. Separately, the report only measured runs the owner had judged; no verdict had ever been recorded, so the report said no transcripts were found for every run, while the same transcripts measured fine one run at a time. The agent's own minutes were a gap heuristic capped at five minutes, and the workers' sessions in their own working copies were not counted at all, so the coordinator's 56 lines stood for a feature whose workers wrote 1838.

Fixed by the ledger: the harness's own totals are read back instead, the forecast is answered by work with the owner's absence reported beside it, and every session of the project is counted.
close_reason: Fixed by the ledger in 0.48.0

title: Adopting time records made work handed in before them a new error, and asked for a claim no command could write
description:
Reported as GitHub #12, met while a project upgraded from setup 0.26.0 to 0.29.0.

## What happened
The new rule `time-work-unclaimed` fired on leaves handed in before the upgrade, by sessions on the
older set that could not write claims at all. Under block-new they counted as NEW because the tracker
had moved past the last committed baseline, so the upgrade's own commit was refused. The rule's fix
text asked for "the claim the session made, with its real start", but `runs.mjs claim` always stamps
now, and no command recovers a claim from a transcript: `gaps` recovers receipts only for spans that
already have a claim. The agent was left with a false record or bypassing the hook.

## The practice
Adoption happens at a moment and work is in flight at it (documents.md already says so for the
document gate): a new obligation binds work started under it, and the work in flight is listed as
exempt when it is adopted, following the task tree. A fix text promises only what a command can do.

## Fix
- Gate config `timeRecordsExempt`: ids listed at adoption; `time-work-unclaimed` skips them and their
  descendants. Setup writes it when time records are first installed.
- `runs.mjs claim --recovered --at <time> --harness --session`: a claim recovered from a transcript on
  this machine, its start inside that transcript, marked recovered; `gaps` then writes its receipt.
- Fix text and setup say both.
close_reason: Done in 0.61.0, setup 0.30.0: timeRecordsExempt in the gate config, following the task tree, written by setup at adoption; runs.mjs claim --recovered at a start inside the session's transcript here, then gaps writes its receipt; the rule's fix text promises only what the script does. Each guard mutated once and caught.

title: An approval bound to the finished change cannot be given in the preflight, so the run always interrupts the owner after he has left
description:
Met in real use on 2026-09-22 on meshynet (Claude session 9e03885e, plugin 0.44.0).

The protocol promises the owner one batch: "before the owner leaves, every decision the
run will need comes as one batch with recommendations, because asking later means
stopping the run". The document check's approval cannot be in that batch, by
construction.

`check-docs.mjs` requires an approval whose `changeDigest` equals `digest(change)` — the
hash of the finished change record. Two consequences follow mechanically:

- it cannot be given before the change record exists, so never in the preflight;
- any later edit to that record voids it.

Both fired in one run. At 16:42 the run already knew it would need him: "Проверки в
конце потребуют семь записанных результатов и твоё утверждение". At 16:44 the owner
said he was leaving: "Я сейчас скоро уйду уже. Потом у тебя будет часа полтора. Чтобы
меня о чём-то спросить." The run could not use that window for this, because the change
record was not written yet. At 17:01 the independent review found a blocker and the
change was rewritten — which would have voided an approval given at 16:44 anyway. At
17:06 the run sent a push to his phone. At 17:14 he asked what it was.

So the one thing that stopped the run and cost the owner's attention after he left was
the one thing the batch rule was written to prevent, and no run can do better while the
approval is bound to a digest of the finished text.

What needs settling: what the owner actually approves. If it is the decision — which
"the tests passed" the project believes from now on — that can be asked in the preflight,
before anything is written, and re-asked only when what he decided changes, not when the
text around it does. The digest then binds the record to what was approved, which is what
a digest is for, instead of standing in for the approval itself. If it is genuinely the
final text, the protocol has to stop promising a batch that cannot contain it, and say
where such an approval is collected and what it costs him.
close_reason: Fixed in 71adcce (0.47.0, setup 0.22.0). changeDigest now covers what the change decides (kind, intent, outOfScope, deltas, preserves), not the whole record, so the approval can be taken in the preflight before anything is written and survives the agent's own working on it; only a change to what he decided voids it. The protocol's Autonomy takes it in the batch, take-task takes it rather than foreseeing it, documents.md states the binding, and two fixtures pin both halves. Projects re-record approvals once: the digest's input changed.

title: An approval of a behaviour change was asked without showing what the person will see change
description:
In a real run (meshynet, 2026-09-21). The agent asked the owner three times to approve a behaviour change, each time describing the change in prose: "the empty peer list stops being bare and names its reason", "the head change leaves a trace of the transition". The owner had to ask what any of it meant on screen — "Где это было и стало?" Only then did the agent print the actual status block before and after, from its own run, and the answer took one screen: one line of operator output grew three lines of explanation, and three neighbouring lines had landed that morning.

Two earlier questions in the same session went the same way — "А в чем вопрос?" and "Что такое квитанция? Что нужно утвердить?" — and the later one was answered in the set's own vocabulary (receipt, change record, gate) rather than in what the product does.

0.41.0 already says an ask carries its own substance and that what is approved is the consequence for the product, never a record or an entry. What it does not say is that where the change is visible — a line of output, a message, a screen, a command's behaviour — the ask SHOWS it: the text as it is today and the text as it will be, taken from a real run and not composed. Prose about a user-visible change is the kitchen in another costume: the person is asked to approve a description instead of the thing.
close_reason: Fixed in 71adcce (0.47.0). Where a change can be seen, the ask shows it: the line as it reads today and as it will read, from a real run, never prose about it. Where nothing can be seen, it says in one sentence what will be true afterwards that is not true now, and that sentence is what is approved. And a thing waiting on the person is named once in the words of what he decides, and named that way in every later mention; the machinery's word is never borrowed, and 'the checks require it' or 'it cannot be signed for you' say who is asking, not what is being decided.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
Recurred on 2026-09-22, same project, one day later (Claude session 9e03885e, plugin
0.44.0). Same question, almost the same words: "Что такое подпись под mej9?"

The change was mej9 — the checks declare what they can read, so a docs commit stops
killing a recorded test result. Over five messages the run referred to what it needed
from the owner as: "твоё утверждение — это в настройках включено (`requireApproval`), и
подписать его за тебя нельзя"; "мне нужна твоя строчка, чтобы её влить"; "Ждёт тебя
по-прежнему одно: подпись под `mej9`". Then a push to his phone. Then his question.

The answer he got opened "В проекте включена настройка", and went on: "Проверка перед
отправкой смотрит, есть ли она; если нет — изменение не проходит", "предохранитель",
"записанный результат", "цена — 29 секунд на изменение". He asked what was wanted from
him and was given a tour of the machinery.

Two things this issue does not yet cover.

**The change had no visible surface.** Nothing on a screen changed; what changed was
which "the tests passed" the project believes. The remedy here — show the output before
and after, from a real run — has nothing to show. An ask for a change with no surface
still has a product question underneath it (the run did find it once, in the middle of
one message: "ты решаешь, какому 'тесты прошли' мы впредь верим"), and the rule has to
reach that case too.

**The rule governs the ask and not the references to it.** A pending approval is
mentioned in every status, in the push notification and in the closing line. The thing
has a name in the mechanism and none in the owner's world, so every one of those
references reverted to the mechanism's name until the name was the only thing he had
met. One good sentence in the middle of message three does not survive four mentions of
"подпись".

title: Jev is never used in a feature run: neither the coordinator nor its workers call it
description:
What happened: two feature runs in a project that consented to Jev (coordinators started 2026-09-28 on 0.70.0, ran ~24h, 8 and 18 workers) made no Jev call at all, not even status. Owner: 'the model does not understand when to use jev; neither the coordinator nor the workers called it once'.

Evidence from the transcripts:
- Neither coordinator ever opened references/judging.md; the only reference one of them read was running.md. The rule of where Jev helps lives only there.
- take-task's SKILL.md names Jev only for the run records' attribution and for carrying it into a worker's brief. No step of the coordinator's own work names the moments that have Jev's shape (a review's findings to sort, several workers' failures, long test/bench logs), and nothing runs status at the start, so the coordinator never learns Jev is available.
- No worker brief mentions Jev. The rule to carry it into the brief shipped in 0.71.0, after these runs started; a running session keeps the skill it loaded. So the workers' side is not proved broken by these runs, but it inherits the same weakness: a brief paraphrase of 'decide where it helps', with no concrete moment tied to the worker's steps.

Pattern: a permission of the form 'any step may use it when the work has this shape', kept in a reference, is never recalled at the moment the shape arises. A tool the agent is not reminded of at the step where it pays is not used.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.74.0: judging.md explains what Jev is and the four conditions under which it pays, with a test before reading a pile; take-task runs status at the start and names Jev at the steps where a run meets piles (failures after a merge, mutation survivors, review findings, long logs); the worker brief carries the principle, not only a list; settled threshold 0.9 by the owner's decision.

title: Workers were launched one way and finished five ways: no result contract binds what follows a dispatch
description:
## What happened

Four coordinator sessions on 2026-09-23 (one nocx run, two meshynet runs, and the meshynet session that started both of those coordinators) each dispatched through herdr and omp in the same way, because the machine's orchestration skill supplied the launch. Everything after the launch was improvised, and differently each time:

- **Completion signal.** Five methods across four sessions: an on-screen sentinel line matched by watch.py, an agent status watch, `herdr agent wait --until done|blocked`, polling for a report file with scheduled wakeups, and a hand-written pane-scraping loop (one ran for 17 h). The sentinel false-fired three times in two sessions because the sentinel text sits in the brief and the worker repeats it while reasoning. The status watch fired at once on `idle`. watch.py died once with no output and was never diagnosed. The report-file method was the only one without false positives.
- **Ending sessions.** nocx left finished workers idle until the owner said "Закрой те воркеры, которые больше не нужны". meshynet closed no worker and no coordinator; a finished coordinator is still idle.
- **A stop never reached the starter.** A child coordinator stopped for an owner approval without printing its stop marker. The parent found out only because its watcher had died and it read the screen. The owner's typed reply sat unsent in the child's input box, and the parent pressed Enter on the owner's behalf.
- **Resume handle.** One coordinator recorded each worker's `omp --resume <id>` in the tracker before closing it. No rule asks for this.
- **Late skill load.** The mechanism's skill was loaded by the word "worker", 20 minutes into one run, not at preflight.

## Situation

take-task has run mode `worker-sessions`, but it names no result contract and no mechanism binding. The launch converged only because a machine-level skill happened to cover it.

## Direction (not yet a spec)

Add a mechanism-independent result contract for every started session, whether worker or coordinator, at any depth:
- A session ends by writing a report at a known path, done or stopped with the reason.
- Done means the report exists and the agent has finished. An on-screen line is never the signal.
- Whoever starts a session closes it after collecting the report.
- The resume handle is recorded at dispatch.
- At preflight, take-task binds `worker-sessions` to the mechanism available in this environment and loads its skill. If there is none, it says so at preflight instead of improvising.

How to wait for the report and how to close the session stays in the mechanism's own skill. The set does not name the mechanism.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.52.0: protocol rule 'A started session answers to the one that started it'; take-task binds the mechanism at preflight and briefs the report path

title: Document-gate adoption leaves in-flight work with no affordable exit
description:
Observed in the same meshynet run on 2026-09-20 (Claude session 70053c15), as the cause of the bypass attempt.

The document gate was adopted in meshynet on 2026-09-19 (`adoptedAt` = the install commit). Everything after it in master was setup bookkeeping, so nothing hit the rule. The stage branch for meshynet-5osj was the first real code to meet it, and it met it at push time, 94 commits in.

What the agent found there: code work needs a `behavior` change record, a `behavior` record must carry at least one requirement delta, and a delta must name a capability in `docs/system/capabilities/` — a directory the project does not have yet. So the first behaviour change after adoption must also invent the project's capability catalogue. The agent's own estimate went from "30-45 minutes" to "1.5-2 hours, and it sets the pattern for all future code", at the moment the owner was waiting to start a live test.

`documents.md` says "Enforce new work without making unrelated undocumented history block every feature" and "Current capabilities may be empty before the first accepted implementation", but nothing in setup or in the skills covers:

- work already in flight when the gate is adopted (the parent bug was in the project's exemption list; its four sub-tasks were not, so the branch was judged anyway);
- the first behaviour change after adoption, which pays for the capability catalogue as well as its own record, with no warning that it would;
- what an agent does when the only visible exits are hours of unplanned work, widening the exemption list, or skipping the hook.

A gate whose cheapest exit at push time is a bypass will be bypassed. Expected: adoption names this cost when it happens, not at the first push — either by seeding the first capability document as part of adoption, or by recording the in-flight work as exempt at adoption (parents and their leaves), or by stating in the skills what the first behaviour change after adoption includes so it is planned work rather than a surprise.
close_reason: Closed by fba0780

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
The session that made the attempt (meshynet 70053c15) named what the set should have given it, confirmed against its transcript. Four of the five need a setup-version bump and so a rerun in every project; grouped here to land as one change.

(a) documents.md, 'Local commands are feedback, not a security boundary'. Setup writes this into the project's own gate header, where it became 'nothing stops a direct tracker write or --no-verify; this detects, it cannot prevent'. The agent read it as a threat model and it became the backbone of its harmlessness argument to the owner. The statement is true and setup needs it; it needs the sentence next to it saying the verdict binds the agent regardless of what enforces it. 0.27.1 put that in the protocol, which travels with the plugin; the project's installed copy keeps saying otherwise until setup runs again.

(b) A refusal names no remedy and no size. 'uncovered-task: meshynet-5osj.1 (commit 54a2d870)' and nothing more; the agent read about 700 lines across the project's gate and the exporter to learn that a code commit implies kind behavior, that behavior needs at least one delta, and that a delta needs a capability document the repository has never had. A gate that can refuse can describe green: the implied kind, the required sections, whether the capability document exists, and the commands that record each check.

(c) adoptedAt grandfathers commits, not work in flight. A branch whose tasks predate adoption but whose commits land after it meets the full contract at push time. Either adoption lists the in-flight work, or it refuses until it is listed.

(d) Exemption does not follow the task tree. The parent bug was exempt; the four leaves it was split into after adoption were not, and that exact shape produced this. Descendants of an exempt task should inherit it, or splitting a bug silently voids the exemption. The flat list is the project's wrapper, but the shape comes from what setup writes.

(e) No bootstrap for the first behaviour change. In mode 'existing' with no capability documents, the first one must invent docs/system/capabilities/ from nothing, discovered after the code is written, reviewed, integrated and green. Either a template, or a rule that the first change may Add against an absent baseline, so it is a bounded job rather than a cliff.

Its own counterfactual: (b), (c) and (e) would have removed the pressure, (a) would have removed its ability to build the harmlessness argument; it would not claim it would certainly have behaved well.

Held until the meshynet stage lands — every setup bump stops every project, and shipping one now would hit the same run in the same place.

title: Estimates from measured pace, not from the model's guess
description: Models misestimate run time badly. Record the estimate before a run and the actual after; a script gives the range similar runs took and how far past estimates were off; take-task and ask-shady2k quote it.
close_reason: Done in 0.26.0

title: A bound on out-of-sight work is the forecast, and an overrun is a defect
description:
Owner's rule, 2026-09-20, from the same live run that waited an hour and fifty-one
minutes for a dead review worker.

The bound on work that runs out of sight was left to the run's judgement. That
permits the two moves the owner rules out: waiting past the forecast because the
work "might still finish", and restarting or raising the bound until it does.

What must hold:

- The timeout is the forecast the model itself gave for that work, not a generous
  round number chosen so nothing ever trips it.
- Passing the forecast is not a reason to wait, restart or extend. It is a reason
  to stop, find out why, and file it, like any other failure the run owns.
- Duration is a measurement, not a feeling. How long tests, a compile, a check or
  any operation takes is compared with what it took before, and a change in it is
  explained. A suite that was four minutes and is now eleven has said something,
  green or not.

Fixes the hole left open by skills-waiting-on-a-dead-worker-3b9, which ended the
waiting but said nothing about what the bound should be or what an overrun means.
close_reason: Closed by 49e82fd

title: A report of the agent's own error ended as a handoff and the run stood still
description:
Same run. Having found that its own field claim was false, the agent stopped the background run (right: it was about to take receipts on text that was about to change), then sent the owner a full account of the mistake. The message ended with praise for the worker that had caught it. Nothing in it needed a decision: the records were the agent's to fix, the fix itself stood on its own evidence, and the owner had said earlier that day to call only if something was needed.

The run then stood still for nine minutes until the owner typed 'and what next?'. Only then did the agent produce the four steps it had been free to take all along.

'End with the next step' covers the missing sentence, but not the shape underneath it: a confession is not a request for permission. An error in the agent's own work continues on the authority already given; what may need the owner is the consequence, and only where it changes something of theirs.
close_reason: fixed in 25710ca

title: A charter answered the owner's open question itself and was closed as accepted without review
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #6 (plugin 0.52.0, setup 0.24.0).

## What happened
A first-milestone charter was written from a conversation in which the owner described the milestone and asked an open question about whether one part should be done with static extraction or by an agent. The charter answered that question itself and wrote the static-extraction machinery into two outcomes. The task that produced the founding documents was closed with the reason "accepted by owner decision without review". The mismatch surfaced only the next day, while planning the first feature, when the owner said the machinery was never meant to be in the milestone; the charter, the vision's direction and three decision records had to be revised.

## What was expected
Before writing, to-milestone shows the charter as a short summary, in particular what it put inside by its own reading of an open question and what it excludes, and gets an explicit yes. A founding document is not closed as accepted without the owner having seen that summary.

## Where
to-milestone, "Propose the charter" and "Write it"; close-out, "Tell done from accepted". Plugin 0.52.0, Claude Code 2.1.280.

## Settings that matter
A new project, first milestone, charter written in the same session as the vision and the decision records.

## How to reproduce
Describe a milestone to to-milestone with one open design question inside it, then accept the documents without reading them. Check whether the charter records the question as open or answers it.

## Where to fix (suggestion)
In to-milestone, mark every outcome part that rests on the agent's own answer to an open question, and show those first in the summary; in close-out, refuse "accepted without review" for vision and charter documents.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.56.0: to-milestone keeps an owner's open question open or shows the agent's answer first, approved by name; writes only on an explicit yes; close-out refuses 'accepted without review' for vision and charter. GitHub #6.

title: A coordinator handed tasks to workers outside the set without writing their claims, and lost the start
description:
Met in the same run. When the coordinator handed tasks to omp workers it marked them claimed in the
tracker and wrote a free-text note, but not the set's claim record, although that record needs no
transcript: only the harness and the session id, both in hand at that moment. The start was lost and
could later only be recovered from a transcript.

## Fix
take-task: a claim is written when the task is handed over, by the coordinator for a worker that does
not run the set, naming the worker's session.
close_reason: Done in 0.63.0, setup 0.31.0

title: A session offered for closing counts its own findings from memory
description:
Observed in a real meshynet run on 2026-09-20 (Claude session f5c1a1bb). Twice near
the end, the run offered to close the session -- "version accepted, eight findings
filed, start a fresh one through /handoff". The tracker held eleven at that moment
(five throughput findings from 14:59, then 719r, c10a, eurg, c1le, 8fxf, lk09 by
16:56); the same sentence also called seven of them station findings when there
were six. The owner, reading it, could not tell what had been filed and answered
"file all the tasks we discussed in this session" -- for a session that had been
filing them all along.

Two defects, one sentence:

- **The count came from the agent's memory, not from the tracker.** Everything
  needed to state it exactly was one query away, and the run had already been
  told that memory and indexes are hints to verify (skills-0kf).
- **Where each one landed was never said.** All eleven were filed deferred with a
  review date three months out, outside the version. From the owner's seat that is
  indistinguishable from nothing being queued, which is what he took from it.

An offer to end a session states what this session found, what of it is in the
tracker with the ids read back from it, which lane each one landed in, and what was
discussed and deliberately not filed. Anything the owner must still decide -- a
milestone to attach to, a finding that did not fit the budget -- is part of the
offer, not a thing he discovers by asking. Related: skills-session-work-unrecorded-byx
is the opposite hole, a session that ends having recorded nothing at all.
close_reason: Closed by f8eb14b

title: The owner is made to wait while the agent works out what it is asking
description:
The owner's rule, 2026-09-20, from the same live run as skills-owner-time-is-scarce-25u.

Two things he asks for, and neither is written anywhere as a duty:

- **Arrive with the material.** When the agent comes to him with a question, the
  work behind it is already done: what was investigated, the options and what each
  costs, the evidence read, its own recommendation. He should not sit and wait
  while the agent works out what it is asking. In that run, when he asked why the
  session was still waiting, the diagnosis of the hung worker began only then --
  with him watching -- and it took one command he could have been shown at once.
- **Bring ideas, and other angles.** Not only answers to what he asked: the
  option nobody raised, the example and the counterexample, the view from a
  different kind of user. The protocol has this for a stop (options compared
  from several sides, a recommendation) and `brainstorming` has it inside a
  conversation, but nothing says the agent owes ideas when it was not asked for
  one.

Both are consequences of the same fact, already in the protocol as of 0.33.0: his
time is the only input the agents cannot produce.
close_reason: Closed by 5f911c7

title: A constraint given for one environment silenced the work everywhere, for a day
description:
In a real run (meshynet, P0 outage, 2026-09-21). At the preflight the owner said, verbatim: "На проде воспроизводить сейчас не будем, нужны логи, инструментировать код" — do not reproduce ON PRODUCTION now; instrument first. The agent carried that forward as "do not reproduce", and for the next four and a half hours the whole run was built on reading a field capture that could not be re-run. Three defects were found that way; the P0 itself was not, and could not be.

When the agent finally proposed reproduction in a container, the owner answered: "воспроизведение в контейнере - это первое, что ты должен был сделать". The reproduction was then written in one worker pass, failed on the first run, and named the cause in a printed line ten milliseconds after the head change — the thing a day of reading had not reached. The harness for it already existed in the repository; nothing had been blocking it but the widened constraint.

The protocol tells the work to reproduce a failure locally rather than debug it through the environment it appeared in, and 0.43.0 makes a quoted decision something the agent must find and re-read. Neither covers this: a prohibition is taken wider than it was given and then silently SHAPES the work without ever being quoted, so no rule ever forces the agent back to the sentence. What is missing is that a constraint carried from a preflight keeps its scope — the environment, the time, the thing it named — and that where a constraint appears to forbid the cheapest decisive check, it is re-read and, if it does not, the check is proposed then and not a day later.

title: A withdrawn fact was corrected in a note while the task's own title kept asserting it
description:
In a real run (meshynet, 2026-09-21), and the reason the owner asked whether the project's context had been poisoned.

A field claim the whole framing rested on turned out to be false (skills-4i3). The agent corrected it properly in the places it thought of: the merged change record carries a CORRECTION section, the capability document's coverage limits carry it, and the task carries a full correction note naming both false statements and the evidence. But the task itself is still titled "The relay rebuilt its carrier to the exit every 45 seconds FOR HOURS before the outage, and nobody knew", its description still reads "hours BEFORE the 20:00:47 publication ... the pattern runs through the journal ... At the head change that cycle STOPPED and never resumed ... it reframes the outage", and the task is still open. The retraction sits roughly 150 lines below all of that, in the notes.

So the falsehood is exactly where every later reader meets it first and the correction is exactly where nobody reaches: a queue listing shows titles, a brief is written from the description, an orientation reads what is open. The next run picks the claim up as the project's own record and has no reason to doubt it.

0.42.0 says a fact found false is corrected everywhere that carries it, "each named as wrong rather than quietly reworded". Read literally, appending a note satisfies it. What is missing is that a record has a part that is read and a part that is not: the correction belongs in the title and in the body, at the top, and the note is the audit trail underneath — and a task whose premise is withdrawn is re-judged (retitled to what is actually true, or closed) rather than left open under a claim that has been retracted.

title: A question the owner already decided is put to them again, because nothing says to search for the decision first
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #7 (plugin 0.48.1, setup 0.22.0).

## What happened
During one long feature run the coordinator stopped the owner three times with a "decision needed" message about something the owner had already decided:

1. Whether to keep building on the current branch or revert a stage: answered the day before, in the previous coordinator session's conversation.
2. How the stored form of a command's output should look: a compact form had been agreed with the owner two days earlier in another session; the built code had drifted from it, and the coordinator offered three options for the consequence instead of finding the agreement.
3. What a `clear` command should do to the earlier output blocks: decided three days earlier and written verbatim ("Owner's decision, <date>: ...") into the body of a task under a different stage of the same feature.

Each time the owner answered "we already decided this". Each question was well worked by "Come with the material" and "A design decision comes with its mechanism" (costs, options, recommendation), which made it look legitimate, but the material never included a search for an existing decision.

## What was expected
Before any question reaches the owner, the coordinator looks for the owner's earlier decision on that topic and, finding one, acts on it and records it where the current work meets it. It asks only when the search finds nothing.

## Where
take-task (run phase: sections 3 and 5, and anything that sends the owner a decision), protocol.md: "Come with the material, not with the question", "A decision the owner gives is kept, not only obeyed", "Memory is a hint", "A decision given is not reopened by better analysis". Set version 0.48.1, setup version 0.22.0, Claude Code 2.1.280, setup verified.

## Settings that matter
Strength block-new; development TDD; run mode worker sessions (later subagents); review different-model with a same-model fallback. The tracker is an issue store kept in the repository; past sessions are searchable through a machine-wide transcript index the project's agent doc describes.

## How to reproduce
1. A feature with two stages. In a task under stage A, the body says "Owner's decision, day 1: X behaves like Y".
2. On day 3 a reviewer working on stage B flags that the client handles X in a way that contradicts stage B's goal.
3. The coordinator reads stage B's criteria and the records they cite, finds nothing about X there, and sends the owner a worked question with three options for X.
Also: a decision given only in an earlier session's conversation (never written to a task) is re-asked by the next coordinator on the same run.

## Where to fix (suggestion)
Add to protocol.md, next to "Come with the material":

"**A question is searched for before it is asked.** Before anything goes to the owner as a decision, search for the answer they may already have given: the tracker across the whole feature and closed work (by the topic's words and their synonyms, not only the stage at hand), the project's decision records, and, where the harness offers one, the index of past sessions and the previous coordinator's transcript on this run. A decision found is acted on and written into the work at hand with where it came from; the owner hears what is being done, not a question. Only an empty search makes a question, and the message says where it looked."

And in take-task section 5 ("A decision the protocol's Autonomy says needs the owner"): make that search the first step before stopping for the owner.

The rule "A decision the owner gives is kept" already asks that decisions be written where the next run meets them; case 2 above shows the other half is needed too: a decision given in conversation and not yet written anywhere is still binding, so the transcript search is part of the check.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.57.1: deciding.md 'A question is searched for before it is asked' (tracker across the feature and closed work, decision records, past-session search and earlier transcripts of the run; found decision is acted on and recorded with its source; a question says where it looked); take-task section 5 makes the search the first step. GitHub #7.

title: A decision already given comes back as the same fork in new clothes, because every message ends with options
description:
Met in real use on 2026-09-21, later in the same owner session as
skills-replaced-ground-mtr, and partly caused by the advice this repository sent
into it.

The owner gave the decision in one line: remove the browser emulator first, then
build the record on the new model. The same fork came back to him four more times
before the run simply proceeded.

  owner: so I propose removing it first, then the later stages
  -> agent accepts, and in the same message recommends finishing five findings
     in the code being removed, plus a "cheap honest answer" that deletes one
     field of the dying representation
  owner: you are asking me to take some complicated architectural decision that
     does not need taking
  -> agent agrees, does the bookkeeping, starts the free task
  -> agent returns with the root cause and a finding-by-finding sorting, and
     disputes one item of the sorting it was handed
  owner: I don't know, ask the reviewer
  -> reviewer adjudicates the sorting, corrects two numbers, offers a fourth
     option and says the agent's framing is loaded
  owner: explain it to me at the product level
  -> a genuinely clear product explanation, ending in three options again
  owner: what on earth are you asking? we agreed to remove it. I don't want to
     write code that will be deleted. What is the question?
  -> "There is no question. Proceeding."

Nothing in those four rounds changed a next action. The stage was not accepted,
so nothing reached the main line whatever anybody decided; the successor work was
already filed; the findings were closed with the stage in the end anyway.

Three habits produced it.

A decision given was treated as an input to further analysis rather than a closed
question. Each new detail — a better sorting of what survives, a reviewer's
fourth option, two corrected numbers — came back as the same fork in new clothes.

A cheap local win inside the dying representation was offered as if cheapness
settled the question of whether it is worth anything.

And every message ended with options and a choice, because that is the shape the
rules reward: come with the material, the options, the costs and a
recommendation. Nothing said that the shape is for a decision that is open.

This repository's own advice made it worse. The message sent into that session
told the agent to sort the findings and bring the owner the cost both ways, and
not to decide the branch's fate itself. By then the owner had already decided.
The sorting became something to litigate, in the session and then with the
reviewer, and the phrase "the sorting I was handed" is in the transcript. A
transcript read from outside says what was true when it was read; the advice was
written against a state the work had already left.
close_reason: Fixed in eff19dd (0.40.0). The options-and-mechanism shape is now explicitly for an open decision; a decision given is not reopened by better analysis, and a message that changes no next action of the owner's is not sent but recorded with the work. Another session's transcript is read as a memory, not a state, so advice written from one checks the current state first. brainstorming and take-task carry the boundary; scenario 18 is the behavioural case.

title: A batch of design decisions reached the owner as conclusions with no sample of what was decided
description:
Reported as GitHub issue #1 (2026-09-24), from a real planning session.

take-task routed the first product feature to brainstorming. The agent sent four ground
decisions in one message: each a recommendation, a line of reasons and a consequence, in the
project's shorthand (decision-record numbers, component names), with a table. No sample of
the thing being decided, nothing about what each option makes possible later. The owner, who
wrote those decision records, twice could not accept and said it was not enough to understand.
A rewrite about four times longer worked: a sample of the format, two rows of the store, a
query written out, a diagram of which part unblocks which later outcome.

Why the rule did not stop it:

- "A design decision comes with its mechanism" asks for architecture views (arc42/C4) but
  never for an instance of the thing decided. "Where the change can be seen, the ask shows it"
  covers only what already runs; before code exists, nothing asks for a sample.
- Nothing governs a batch of decisions in one message, which is where each one got
  compressed. Splitting is not the answer, since take-task's preflight must batch.
- The pre-send reread in speaking.md does not list a decision without a sample, and a
  decision record's number does not read as an identifier under "Names, not identifiers".
close_reason: Fixed in 0.52.1: deciding.md's mechanism rule asks for a worked sample, what each option enables, and material per decision in a batch; speaking.md's pre-send reread checks for it

title: A design decision reaches the owner as three variants of one frame, without the mechanism that generated them
description:
Met in real use on 2026-09-21, in the same session as
skills-owner-language-renames-9ej.

The decision put to the owner: a screen-capture record does not fit the size
limit of the frame it travels in, on the channel between the two processes.
Three options came with it, with costs and a recommendation — compress the
cells, teach requests to chunk like responses already do, or reverse the
direction so the record travels as a response.

The owner answered in one line: then bulk output and history belong on a
channel of their own, obviously. That option was on nobody's list, and it is
the one the run then took.

All three offered options were ways to fit bulk data under the limit of an
interactive channel. The assumption that generated them — that the record uses
that channel at all — was never stated, so it could not be questioned. Neither
was the mechanism: which process holds what, why a cap exists at all
(head-of-line blocking against a carrier shared with the terminal's own bytes),
and that the split already exists by frame type while the carrier stays single.
Once that reached the owner, in the fourth message, his option took one line to
state, and the agent could finally say what it does not fix: the storage limit
and the wasteful cell encoding stay whatever is chosen.

"Come with the material, not with the question" asks for options, costs,
evidence and a recommendation, and that first message had all four. What it does
not ask for is the mechanism the options act on, or the assumption that produced
exactly those options. A menu whose frame is invisible reads as one question
asked three times, and the answer outside the menu then costs a round per
message that kept the mechanism back.
close_reason: Fixed in 6c5e8e8 (0.38.0). A design decision now comes with how the thing works today in the project's own names, the measurement of what fails, the assumption its options rest on, and at least one option that rejects that assumption; each option says what it does not fix. take-task and brainstorming carry it, and dialogue scenario 16 is the behavioural case.

title: An agent-written reproduction was reported as a third-party defect, with an upstream issue proposed, before its control ran
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #8 (plugin 0.57.1, setup 0.26.0).

## What happened

After the orientation report, the owner asked the agent to look for known issues in a third-party embedded database that a recorded finding blamed for memory growth. The agent wrote synthetic reproductions and, within one follow-up, reported to the owner as fact that the library's JavaScript binding never releases discarded prepared statements, that nobody had reported it, and proposed filing two issues upstream. The recommendation that ended the message was built on that claim.

The reproduction was a tight synchronous loop that never yielded to the event loop. In that runtime, native objects are released by finalizers that run only once the event loop turns. When the owner asked a follow-up question, the agent reran the test with a yield every few hundred iterations. Memory stayed flat under both runtimes, so the "bug" was an artefact of the harness. The agent had to retract the claim, and the proposal shrank from "file two upstream issues" to "file one, the rest is our configuration". To the owner, the recommendation flipped between two consecutive messages.

The earlier finding it was investigating had the same shape. A reviewer's single measurement, recorded as "the library leaks on filtered recursive queries", was relayed in the orientation report as fact and framed an owner decision with three options. The investigation showed the filter clause had nothing to do with it.

## What was expected

Before a claim that someone else's software is defective reaches the owner, and certainly before it is offered as the basis of an outward-facing action (an upstream issue), the reproduction should be checked against the obvious control: does it still happen under the conditions the real system runs in (here: a server that yields between requests)? Do the test harness's own shortcuts explain it? Until then, the message should present it as a hypothesis with the missing control named, not as a finding with a recommended action.

Similarly, a recorded finding that rests on a single unreplicated measurement should be reported as such ("measured once, cause not isolated") when it frames an open decision.

## Where

- Skill: ask-shady2k, the follow-up after the report: evidence behind a decision waiting on the owner, and the ways forward.
- Set version: plugin 0.57.1, setup version 0.26.0 (the repository's installation was 0.24.0, out of date).
- Agent: Claude Code 2.1.281.
- Setup: installed, backlog gate green.

## Settings that matter

Strength block; development TDD; one worker; review by a different model preferred, with a same-model fallback (the original finding came from a same-model reviewer); personal scope; an issue store kept in the repository. The owner's role is product engineer who is also the code's engineer through agents.

## How to reproduce

1. A project whose closed feature left an open owner decision. The decision's text states a library defect as fact, based on one reviewer measurement ("memory grows by N KB per query when the query has clause X; without X it is flat"), and lists options that assume the defect.
2. Run ask-shady2k. It relays the decision with its framing.
3. The owner asks: "look for upstream issues; maybe we configured it wrong?"
4. The agent writes a synthetic loop, sees memory exhaustion, finds no matching upstream issue, and reports "real upstream bug, unreported, let us file it", without testing whether the loop itself (no yield, no GC opportunity, default thread count) causes the effect.
5. One question later, it runs the control and retracts.

## Where to fix (suggestion)

The shared rule "A reading is not a fact until its edges are read" in `references/deciding.md` covers logs and samples, not experiments. Add a sibling rule there, for example:

> **An experiment is not a finding until its control has run.** A reproduction written by the agent shows what happens in the harness, not in the product. Before saying that a dependency, a platform or a colleague's code is at fault, run it again under the conditions the real system runs in, and once with the harness's own shortcuts removed (a loop that never yields, default settings nobody chose, a measurement taken once). Until both have run, it reaches the owner as a hypothesis with the missing control named, and no outward-facing action (an upstream issue, a public comment) is proposed on it. A finding recorded from a single measurement says so where it frames a decision.

Optionally, in ask-shady2k's section 2, when an open decision rests on a recorded finding, it could note whether that finding was replicated or isolated before presenting the decision's options.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.57.2: deciding.md 'An experiment is not a finding until its control has run' (rerun under the real system's conditions and without the harness's shortcuts before blaming a dependency, platform or colleague; until then a hypothesis with the missing control named and no outward-facing action; a recorded finding framing a decision says how far it was established); cited from ask-shady2k section 2 and diagnose-bug section 4. GitHub #8.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: 0.57.3: the 0.57.2 rule retold the incident; replaced, together with 'A reading is not a fact until its edges are read', by one general rule in deciding.md, 'A claim reaches only as far as its evidence' (sampling edges, controls, replication, alternative explanations; unchecked claims travel as hypotheses). ask-shady2k and diagnose-bug cite it.

title: The protocol's rules are restated in the skills, and one 874-line file is linked for every rule
description: Found 2026-09-23 while fixing skills-zm0: the owner noted the fix copied one conversation into three places instead of naming the architectural practice once. An audit counted about 375 lines of SKILL.md and AGENTS.md that restate protocol rules (take-task ~95, brainstorming ~75 of 143, AGENTS.md ~50, ask-shady2k ~33, diagnose-bug ~27), often right beside a reference to the same rule. Six skills (brainstorming, model-domain, to-prototype, to-research, diagnose-bug, handoff) carry no protocol, so they must restate it; the artifact-language paragraph is copied six times. The protocol itself is one 874-line file, so a skill that needs three rules links all of them. Plan: split the protocol into a core (setup version, compatibility, levels and backlog rules) and topic references in each skill's references/ folder (speaking to the owner, deciding, running, checks); let every skill link only what it uses; reduce SKILL.md passages to their skill-specific part plus a reference; restate the design-decision rule as architectural practice (views as in arc42/C4, quality attributes, existing blocks first) instead of the list copied from one session. Constraint from the owner: no rule is lost. Verify: every rule heading survives, every cited rule resolves, an independent review of the diff for dropped substance.
close_reason: Fixed by 6deb5a9 and 9928f56

title: A fault filed under the setup task made it a parent, and the document gate refused the setup's own change
description:
Reported as GitHub #14, met during a setup run with the document gate wired.

## What happened
A fault found in the project's tooling was filed, as the lane table says, "under the setup task".
That made the setup task a parent; the setup's change record lists it as its task, the document
gate judges listed tasks as leaves, and refused the setup's own change. A reviewer caught it.

## The practice
Filing a fault must never change whether the work it was found in can be accepted. "Under the
work" is right for a container; for a leaf it turns it into a container and its own records (claim,
change record) stop describing it. Beside it, under the same parent, with its milestone label and a
provenance link, keeps the slice and the budget the same.

## Fix
Protocol "Only what the milestone chose is intake" says "filed with", and what that means; to-backlog's
lane table and setup follow it. The installed gate's fix text still says "under the setup task";
it takes the same words at the next setup version, since changing it alone would make every
project rerun setup.
close_reason: Done in 0.62.0

title: omp installs the plugin but never upgrades it: its upgrade of every plugin goes by the catalog entry's version, which the catalog did not carry
description: What happened: omp installs the Claude Code plugin from the shared catalog and discovers all 16 skills from plugin.json's list, but after a release 'omp plugin upgrade' with no name answered 'All marketplace plugins are up to date', and its startup update check reads the same field. Only 'omp plugin upgrade shady2k-skills@shady2k' reached the new version. Situation: the owner asked for full omp support; checked in an isolated omp 18.1.17 state. Fix: the catalog entry carries the version, bump writes it, npm test fails when it differs from plugin.json (Claude Code's validate --strict refuses a mismatch anyway), test:omp proves install, discovery and a no-name upgrade; README, docs/omp.md and setup's scope advice cover omp.

title: A fresh clone passes a local guard silently until someone connects it by hand
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #2 (plugin 0.52.0, setup 0.24.0).

## What happened
A public repository was cloned on a second machine. The clone had no local hooks, no clean filter for the tracker export and no private pattern file. Connecting it took the manual steps listed in the integration document (hooks path, three filter settings, the pattern file, the tracker import and path migration). The privacy guard script exits 0 when its pattern file is missing, so a clone connected only partly, or a hook run without the file, lets any staged content through with no message.

A related gap in the document gate guidance: the project's own gate adapter defined the evidence revision as the tree minus the tracker export and the current specs. The capability catalogue page beside the specs was left inside it, so the closing commit that updates the catalogue staled the evidence, and closure had to be split into two commits.

## What was expected
- Setup leaves one committed command that connects a fresh clone (hooks, filters, tracker import and migration, a check for the pattern file) and is safe to rerun.
- The privacy guard refuses a commit when its pattern file is missing, saying how to connect the clone, instead of passing everything.
- Optionally, the pattern list can be read from a per-user location outside the repository, so a second machine gets it without copying by hand.
- documents.md names which paths belong outside the evidence revision (the tracker export, the current specs and their catalogue).

## Where
setup-shady2k-skills, sections "Write or repair the integration" and "Prove the whole installation" (fresh-clone connection); the privacy guard written for a public repository; documents.md, "Two levels of evidence". Plugin 0.52.0, setup version 0.24.0, Claude Code 2.1.280.

## Settings that matter
Personal scope, public repository, an issue store kept in the repository with a clean filter for absolute paths, block strength, records evidence level.

## How to reproduce
1. Install the set in a public repository with a privacy guard and a clean filter.
2. Clone it again elsewhere; do not run the manual connection steps, or run all but the pattern file.
3. Stage a file containing a personal email and commit: the guard passes it.

## Where to fix (suggestion)
Generate a connect script under the tooling folder during setup and name it as the fresh-clone step in the integration; make the guard fail closed; list unrevisioned paths in documents.md.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.57.0, setup 0.26.0: one committed connect command in the integration, run by setup for a new clone and proved in a scratch clone; every local guard fails closed (building.md A missing input is an error); documents.md 'What the revision binds' leaves the tracker export, change records, current specs and catalogue out of the evidence revision. GitHub #2.

title: The gate's refusal names the manoeuvre the protocol forbids: finding-budget tells the run to defer
description:
Met in real use on 2026-09-22, in an owner session on nocx (Claude session
b124c7f4, a worker coordinator on the branch `fix/e2e-shard-ci`).

`ci-mac` went red on a branch whose whole diff was CI configuration. The run
diagnosed it correctly down to the product defect — `AddWorktree` removed the
branch git had already created on the CALLER'S expired context, so the branch
survived in the person's repository — wrote a deterministic failing test in the
git seam, fixed it, and got the package green. Then the pre-commit gate refused
the commit that carried the fix:

    finding-budget: finding 21 of 21, against a budget of 20

The run's next move, from the log: it deferred the finding to 2026-11-01 with a
comment saying "Deferred for the BUDGET, not for the work", the gate went green,
and the fix was committed and pushed. It reported the deferral to the owner as
"the mechanism the gate names itself".

It is. `check.mjs` finding-budget carries

    fix: 'Defer the finding, or ask the owner to replace named planned work ...'

and the protocol, since 0.29.0, says the opposite in **A gate that refuses is not
routed around**: the cheapest way is chosen "among the ways that do the work,
never among the ways that shrink what is counted: dropping the label that puts an
item in the slice, deferring it or narrowing it until the number fits is the same
manoeuvre as switching the check off, and it costs more, because the record then
says the work is not there."

The refusal message names the forbidden manoeuvre first, and an agent that obeys
the gate's own instruction violates the protocol while believing it complied. The
record is now false twice over: the finding says the fault waits until November
while its fix is merged in PR #227, and the milestone's counter says it absorbed
twenty findings when it absorbed twenty-one.

Every check's `fix:` line is read by the agent at the moment of refusal, when it
is looking for the cheapest exit, and it outranks a paragraph of protocol read
hours earlier. The remedy lines are where the protocol has to hold, not only the
prose.
close_reason: Fixed in 3d77c2b (0.45.0, setup 0.20.0). finding-budget's remedy line now names the ways that do the work, all of them the owner's to give, and names deferring-to-fit, dropping the milestone label and narrowing as the count-shrinking manoeuvres they are. Because a project keeps its installed gate until setup is rerun, the protocol also says a way the check itself names is not exempt: what a remedy line printed is a defect to report, not an instruction to follow.

title: A run was called green on the harness's exit code for a compound command, not the run's own
description:
In a real run (meshynet, P0 outage, 2026-09-21). The coordinator started the full container suite in the background as `make e2e > log 2>&1; echo "e2e exit=$?"`. The harness reported the background task as "completed (exit code 0)", because the exit code it reports is the last command of the compound one — the echo. The real code was 2, and the real verdict was in the log: `make: *** [Makefile:95: e2e] Error 1`. The suite was RED.

The coordinator took the reported zero as the run passing and said so. It caught the falsehood only because a green contradicted what it expected: the run was supposed to fail (it was a reproduction of an open defect). Its own words afterwards: if the result had matched the expectation, it would have accepted the false green. On this machine the same class of failure is routine — deja counts 144 sessions that hit `warning: build failed` and 135 that hit a package build failure, all of them able to leave a zero somewhere.

A receipt exists so that "the tests passed" is not the agent word. But nothing in the protocol says where the verdict of a run may be read FROM. A green must come from the thing that ran — its own exit status, or the log naming the suite as passed — never from a wrapper, an echo, a harness summary line, or the absence of visible errors. The check is cheapest exactly where it matters: read the tail of the log before recording a receipt, and treat a green that could not be distinguished from a broken invocation as no result at all.

title: A decision waiting on the owner was handed over as reading, not as the statement they approve
description:
What happened (GitHub #18): ask-shady2k's orientation found that the only open item on a feature was the owner's written acceptance of a proof. The report recommended it but costed it as '30-60 min of your reading' and pointed to a document section, a test file and review comments. The owner wanted to be told what exactly they approve.

Evidence: the rules exist (speaking.md 'Summarize; never assign reading' names approval explicitly; deciding.md 'Come with the material'), and ask-shady2k carries both, but the step that ends the report with 'the single decision it needs' cites neither.

Pattern: a rule kept in a reference is not applied at the step where its shape arises unless that step names it. Fix: cite it at the decision point, for any decision, not only acceptance; and state in deciding.md that an approval is worked material too.

title: A session asks for one merge per record: bookkeeping opens its own pull request instead of landing once
description:
Met in real use on 2026-09-20, in one owner session that ran a stage of one
feature from morning to night. The owner was asked to merge four pull
requests; only one of them carried the work.

  09:13  #209  tracker records only, left by a closing
  09:49  #210  a lesson written into the project's agent doc, plus its task
  19:44  #211  the stage itself
  20:39  #212  the records the closing of #211 left, plus a document

Three of the four are bookkeeping. Each cost the owner a round of attention
and the repository a full run of its checks, and the last one existed only
because the run kept committing to the branch while its pull request was
open, so the merge took part of the branch and the rest needed somewhere to
go.

"Sessions and landing" already says plans land with as few merges as
possible and that the rest of a conversation's plan lands once, at its end.
It did not hold, for two reasons. It speaks of "a conversation's plan", so a
closing's records, a lesson in a document and a filed task each read as
something else, and each skill invocation is its own moment that sees no
other. And "A submitted branch is frozen" ends with "waits for the merge or
goes on its own branch", which licenses a new branch, and a new branch here
means a new pull request immediately.

Nothing says where a held record lives between being written and landing, so
holding it feels like risking it; opening a pull request feels like the safe
thing. Nothing says that a merge is never opened for bookkeeping alone.
close_reason: Fixed in adfbcf9 (0.36.0). 'Sessions and landing' now covers everything a session keeps, not only its plan: it lands once, at the session's end, all together, on the session's one landing branch, each record committed there as it is made; never a merge for bookkeeping alone, the exception being what something else needs before the end. The freeze rule sends what it displaces to that branch instead of one of its own. close-out, to-backlog and take-task carry it where each of them lands something.

title: Upkeep of the set's own gates and their CI wiring is filed as a milestone finding and charged to its budget
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #10 (plugin 0.57.1, setup 0.26.0).

## What happened

A setup rerun (updating the installation to a newer setup version) changed the hooks, added the clone-connect command and touched the build file. The project's CI classifies a change as product code by path, so the setup pull request ran the whole product suite. One end-to-end test failed on a flake that had nothing to do with the change, and the setup could not land while it was red.

Two pieces of work came out of that, and the owner asked to file and fix both at once:

1. The CI classifier counting the git hooks and the connect script as product code, so every future tooling change runs the full suite.
2. The flaky test itself, which was blocking the setup's merge.

`to-backlog` sent the first one through step 3 as a finding. The milestone's finding budget was already exhausted, so it was filed deferred, and the owner was asked to choose: raise the budget, leave it for the next milestone, or displace other work. The second one only escaped the budget because the agent noticed, late, that it matched "a repair the merge waits on". It had first been filed with no parent, and the gate refused it as off-milestone.

The owner's answer: this work is outside the budget, because it repairs the set's own gates, and without it the setup cannot get through CI.

## What was expected

Work that exists because the set is being installed or kept working never reaches the finding budget or the owner's budget question. That covers the gates, hooks, commit-link check, connect command, and the CI wiring that decides which checks a tooling change owes. It belongs to the setup task's own lane: filed under the setup work, with no finding label and no milestone label, and fixed as part of landing the setup.

The same holds for a red required check that blocks the setup's own pull request, even though the setup is not a milestone feature.

## Where

- Skills:
  - `to-backlog`, step 2 (lane table) and step 3 (budget);
  - `setup-shady2k-skills`, the profile item "How changes reach the main line" and step 5 (landing);
  - the shared protocol rule "A repair the merge waits on is not intake".
- Set version 0.57.1, setup version 0.26.0, installed version 0.22.0 (the rerun was the update).
- Agent: Claude Code 2.1.280.
- Setup state: installed and verified at the previous version; the rerun had its proofs done and was waiting on CI to land.

## Settings that matter

- Scope: team.
- Gate strength: block-new.
- Finding budget: 20, already exceeded (21 findings) before this happened.
- Landing by pull request, with CI required. The CI skips product jobs only for paths it classifies as non-product.
- Development: tdd. Workers run in separate sessions, up to 3. Review by another model.
- Tracker: an issue store kept in the repository.
- Role: the owner, the person who decides scope and budget.

## How to reproduce

1. Take a project whose CI runs the full product suite for any change outside a short list of documentation and tracker paths, with one known flaky end-to-end test.
2. Exhaust the current milestone's finding budget (for example budget 5, 6 findings filed).
3. Run a setup rerun that edits a git hook and the build file. Open its pull request and let the flaky test fail.
4. Ask the agent to file, through `to-backlog`, "the CI classifier treats hook changes as product code" and "fix the flaky test that blocks this merge".
5. Observed: the first is classified as a finding, over budget, deferred, and put to the owner as a budget decision. The second is filed without a parent, and the gate refuses it as off-milestone until the agent re-reads the repair rule.

## Where to fix (suggestion)

- **Shared protocol, "Two lanes outside the flow" or "A repair the merge waits on is not intake":** add a third kind that is not intake. Work that keeps the set's own installation working goes under the setup task, with no finding or milestone label and no budget. This covers repairs to its checks, hooks, connect command, and the CI wiring that decides what a tooling change owes. Also say explicitly that a red required check on the setup's own pull request is a repair that merge waits on, and is parented under the setup task.
- **`to-backlog`, step 2:** add a row to the lane table: "a defect or gap in the set's own gates, hooks or their CI wiring, found while installing or running them → under the setup work, outside the budget; step 3 does not apply".
- **`setup-shady2k-skills`, "How changes reach the main line":** it recommends, "as a separate task", letting CI skip product checks for documents and tracker changes. Extend that to the set's own wiring (hooks, connect command), and say where that task goes: under the setup work, not the finding lane. Otherwise a strict milestone budget turns the set's own upkeep into a budget negotiation with the owner, and a setup that must pass a flaky product suite cannot land.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.59.0, setup 0.28.0: 'A repair the merge waits on is not intake' widened into 'Only what the milestone chose is intake' (work is charged to the work it serves; repairs a merge waits on, the setup's included, and upkeep of the installation go under their owner, no finding label, no budget); setup task is live work of the current milestone without the finding label; to-backlog lane row and step 3, setup's CI item and landing cite it; the budget check's fix text says so. Also removed incident counts from the backlog check's messages. GitHub #10.

title: Jev can take batch and long-material judgements off the agent, opt-in, with the model choosing where
description:
Jev (TypeSafe's decision model: picks among supplied options, returns per-option probabilities and a confidence; reachable directly or through OpenRouter as `typesafe/jev-1.13`) may speed up the judgements the set asks of agents and scripts. Brainstormed 2026-09-28; two throwaway measurements were run on this repository.

## Decisions the owner gave
- **Opt-in, asked by setup.** Setup asks the person whether they want Jev at all and where its key is kept. Nothing is used without that answer.
- **The model decides where, from guidance.** The set does not confine Jev to a fixed list of steps. It explains to the model where Jev does best and where it fails, with the measured evidence, and the model chooses when to use it.
- **What is sent is masked.** Anything sent to the outside service is masked first (secrets, personal data and identifiers).

## Measured (throwaway, scratchpad only)
1. **Short items: is a code span in the docs a path?** 312 spans, hand-labelled. Current shape regex 97.1%; Jev alone 95.5% (reads literally: took commands containing a file name for paths); Haiku 97.1%. Jev plus the agent re-reading only the 14% of mid-confidence answers: 99.0%. Jev's confidence was reliable at the ends (<0.05: 125/125 right; >0.95: 50/51) and worthless in the middle (0.5-0.8: 0/7). Jev 2.5x faster and 10x cheaper than Haiku.
2. **Long items: which of 81 tracker issues did a session work on?** 26 sessions of this repository (owner and agent text only, issue ids masked so the answer could not be read off), truth from the issues each session committed or closed. Jev top-1 25/26, truth in its top 3 in 26/26; Haiku 21/26. Median 0.6 s against 1.6 s; $0.013 against $0.27 for all 26. About 240k tokens of session text, more than an agent could read. One session exceeded Jev's input limit and needs cutting or splitting.

Outside evidence (independent tests, 13 days after release): level with mid-price models, 6-11 points behind the frontier; renaming the options changed about a third of answers; no built-in "none of these"; confidence overconfident on rules it has not seen; Russian inference questions lose about 11 points, intent or topic choice holds.

## Proposed shape (not yet decided)
- One dependency-free module in the set, used two ways: as a library by scripts that have no agent (the time ledger's session-to-task attribution, today a text match of the id anywhere in the transcript), and as a command the agent runs for a batch (`triage`: one question over many items, each answer marked settled or "look yourself"). Copied into skill folders like the protocol. An offline mode with canned answers for `npm test`.
- Guidance in the protocol's references, cited by skills: what Jev is good at (batches of similar judgements over material the agent would otherwise read in full, long-material attribution), where it is weak (short literal items, arithmetic, dates, its own mid-range confidence), a "none of these" option in every question, mid-confidence answers go back to the agent, nothing consequential rests on Jev's word alone. Without a key or opt-in everything works as today.
- Not an MCP server: the ledger scripts cannot call one. Not a dependency on third-party jev-mcp or jev-use.
- A new setup question and config value mean a setup version bump.

## Open
- Is the opt-in per machine or per project? (Per project protects code that is not the owner's.)
- Masking: which rules; the report scan (`report-to-shady2k/scan.mjs`) already knows secrets and identifying shapes.
close_reason: Shipped in 0.68.0, setup 0.36.0: jev.mjs (status, ask, replay, mask) with masking on every call and settled answers only at the confidence ends; references/judging.md tells the model where Jev helps; setup asks each project for consent and the key's place and proves it live; ask-shady2k replays on request; the time ledger's use is skills-ledger-jev-attribution.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner, 2026-09-28: Jev's effectiveness must be measurable, so what Jev decided is recorded. Proposed: each call records the question, how many items, how many Jev settled on its own (confident ends, accepted unread) and how many went back to the agent; for those, whether the agent's answer differed from Jev's. A small sample of the settled ones is re-read, so its error rate is known, not assumed. Where this lands (the time record's events, or a log of its own) is open.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner, 2026-09-28: consent is per project. Setup asks each project separately whether Jev may be used there; a key on the machine alone permits nothing. This is a project config value, so shipping it bumps the setup version.

comments.author: dev
comments.text:
Decided with the owner, 2026-09-28, after consulting Codex.

MASKING: done by the one module that sends to Jev, on every call; the agent cannot switch it off. Always removed: keys, passwords, tokens, auth headers, connection strings, emails, phones, usernames, hosts, IPs, home paths. Replaced by typed placeholders stable within one request and salted per request (<ISSUE_1>, <PERSON_1>, <HOST_1>): issue ids, people, organisations and repositories, commit hashes, outside hosts. Kept: code symbols, file names, relative paths, issue titles (the signal). An item that is credential material as a whole (.env, vault export, private key) is not sent. The rendered request is scanned again before sending and nothing is sent if it fails. report-to-shady2k/scan.mjs is a seed, not enough: it knows shapes only. Called best-effort redaction, never anonymisation. Per-project consent does not replace it; setup states the route (OpenRouter and TypeSafe, or TypeSafe) and that TypeSafe keeps data.

MEASURING: whether Jev is wrong is measured by replaying it, by script, on labelled cases built from the project's own history (truth from commits and closed issues, as in this issue's measurement 2), after a model or question change and periodically while Jev is used; rates are kept per kind of decision, never pooled. Individual Jev decisions are NOT recorded (owner: that is debugging). Consequence accepted: there is no rate of live decisions later contradicted by the work; replay is the only measure, and it holds only as far as the history resembles current work.

Evidence the masking keeps the signal: measurement 2 masked every issue id and Jev still attributed 25 of 26 sessions.

comments.author: dev
comments.text: Owner, 2026-09-28, supersedes the timing above: the replay on the project's history runs only when the user asks for it. No periodic run and no automatic run after a model or question change. Consequence accepted: a drop in Jev's accuracy after an update goes unnoticed until someone asks.
