title: A run waits on a delegated worker that never started
description:
Observed in a real run on 2026-09-20 (Claude session 32ba7716, a feature stage in
a worktree). The coordinator dispatched the second review to another agent and
then waited 1 hour 51 minutes without checking anything. Its own status line said
the review had been going "over an hour" and it still waited. The owner ended it
with "And? Are we still waiting? Does that not strike you as strange?"

The worker had been dead from the start: 0.17 seconds of processor time in 68
minutes, asleep in a futex, no transcript of its own ever created, while the
first round of the same review had taken 26 minutes. One command showed all of
that once it was finally run, and a fresh worker answered a smoke test in
seconds.

Three things made the hour and a half possible, and all three are ours to fix:

- **No bound.** The call had no timeout. Nothing would ever have ended the wait.
- **A pipe that hid the truth.** The output went through `tail -200`, which holds
  everything until the end, so zero bytes looked like "reading slowly" instead of
  "never started".
- **Silence taken for work.** Elapsed time well past what the same review took
  before was treated as news about the review's difficulty rather than as a
  reason to look. The cheap checks -- processor time, an output file growing, the
  worker's own transcript -- cost seconds and were run only after the owner asked.

The run's own words afterwards: "I took silence for work for too long. I should
have looked at processor time on the first check."

Related: skills-run-stalls-in-silence-tbq is the same failure seen from the other
side, where it is the run itself that stops and nobody learns.
close_reason: Closed by 83bc738

title: A worker's broad add committed the coordinator's uncommitted tracker change under the worker's task
description:
Reported from real use as GitHub issue #5 (plugin 0.52.0, setup 0.24.0).

## What happened
While a worker was implementing a task, the coordinator filed a new issue in the tracker kept in the repository, which changed its export file in the working tree. The worker, told not to touch the tracker, committed with a broad add, so its commit carried the coordinator's tracker change under the worker's task link. Earlier workers in the same run noticed the modified export and left it alone; this one did not.

## What was expected
Workers stage only the paths they changed, or the coordinator never leaves its own uncommitted changes in a checkout a worker commits in.

## Where
take-task, "Run the feature" (what each worker is given; shared checkouts). Plugin 0.52.0, Claude Code 2.1.280.

## Settings that matter
One worker working in the coordinator's checkout (no separate working copy), tracker export versioned in the repository.

## How to reproduce
1. Dispatch a worker in the coordinator's checkout.
2. While it works, make a tracker write from the coordinator.
3. The worker commits with `git add -A`: the tracker change rides in its commit.

## Where to fix (suggestion)
Add "stage only your own paths" to what workers are told, and "commit or stash your own changes before dispatching into a shared checkout" to the coordinator's steps.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.56.0: take-task 'A worker commits only its own paths'; the coordinator commits its own changes before dispatching into its checkout. GitHub #5.

title: The document gate demands a change record for filing a task, and empty records are signed to feed it
description:
Observed in a real meshynet session on 2026-09-24 (Claude session fbc43909), plugin 0.54.0, setup 0.24.0.

The owner said "push first, then open the milestone". Local master held tracker-only commits that filed four findings (open tasks, on a milestone not yet opened). The project's document-gate wrapper refused the push with `uncovered-task`: its range check treats every open task a commit names as work that commit implements, and demands a change record with the owner's approval for it. Filing a task or commenting on it implements nothing.

How it had been handled before: twice, an agent wrote an empty change record ("found and filed, nothing fixed") and had the owner sign it, so the push would pass. This time the agent proposed the same, recommending it, and listed "push around the check" as option 2 with a "I would not". The owner called the demand absurd and had the check fixed.

The fix (in the project's wrapper): a tracker-only commit needs no change record for a task nothing has been delivered on by the tip; one that moves a task to submitted, implemented or closed without a change stays refused. The first version exempted everything but `closed`; another model's review found that a tracker-only commit could mark a task implemented with no change behind it.

Why it is the set's: the wrapper is written by setup from documents.md, which says what a change record is but not which commits owe one. Any project whose wrapper is written again can make the same mistake. And "A gate that refuses is not routed around" does not name the empty record written only to satisfy the check as routing around, although it trains the owner's signature to mean nothing.

Also seen: the agent put a file path and line numbers of the gate in front of the owner.

Expected: documents.md states that a commit owes a change record for what it delivers (code, documents, a tracker transition to a delivered state), not for the tasks it names; checks.md says an empty record fed to a check is routing around it, and a check that demands what the work does not owe is a defect to fix.
close_reason: Fixed in 0.55.0: documents.md 'A commit owes a record for what it delivers' (the wrapper's range line drawn at delivered states, proved both ways); checks.md names the empty record fed to a check as routing around it. Setup 0.25.0.

title: ask-shady2k waits indefinitely when one delegated evidence response stalls
description:
Observed in omp session 01a0f6df-ae3e-7593-bbfd-48f989996a05 on 2026-10-01 with plugin 0.79.0. The main openai-codex/gpt-6-sol run invoked ask-shady2k and delegated tracker evidence to openai-codex/gpt-6-luna:low. The worker completed 37 sequential read/search/shell calls in 99 seconds. Its last completed model turn had 88,977 tokens of context and asked for `br list -s in_progress --json`; that command returned in 0.06 seconds. The next OpenAI response (`resp_0a48b07da3cb966c016abe2e2efa6c87d1bd4fb8ede2fadb4a`) never produced a transcript record. Omp accepted steering into that same response at 13:01, 13:06, 13:13 and 13:17 local time, proving one response stayed in flight for more than 21 minutes.

The main session remained responsive and issued 18 one-minute waits. The independent product-evidence worker completed, but after 27 minutes the owner still had no orientation. The parent had already collected enough verified branch and repository evidence for a bounded answer. The failure is therefore two-layered: one OpenAI worker response stalled after a large evidence context, and ask-shady2k has no bounded fallback that returns verified facts while naming the unavailable collector evidence as unknown. This capture does not show general OpenAI API latency: the preceding 37 worker turns and the parent OpenAI turns completed normally.

Expected: ask-shady2k returns a decision-oriented orientation once decision-critical evidence is available; one stalled optional collector cannot hold the owner indefinitely. Observable criterion: in a harness where one delegated evidence response never settles after other decision-critical evidence is available, the owner receives the orientation from verified evidence and the missing fields are explicit. Disproof: the main session keeps issuing waits for that collector and emits no answer.

Deliberately left out: changing omp model routing or claiming a provider-wide OpenAI performance defect. The capture establishes one stalled response and missing orchestration fallback, not its upstream transport cause.

title: A worker's session is left running after its result is merged, and holds memory until the owner notices
description: Happened 2026-09-23 in a take-task run coordinating omp workers in separate terminal panes (session f10a3db0). The coordinator merged five workers' results into the feature branch over the day and ended none of them; each idle agent kept its process and memory. title: A design question is put to the owner without the boundaries of the parts it touches, and the owner has to ask for them round after round
description: Happened 2026-09-23 in the same take-task run (session f10a3db0). Deciding where a command block's output is kept, the coordinator offered three options, all copying lines, when the terminal emulator's own scrollback already held them; the owner pointed that out. It then described a line-range scheme; the owner asked to explain it higher-level, then 'tell me the boundaries of each part: where and what is processed', then 'what happens when the coordinator is unavailable'. Only after those three rounds did the answer show, per part, where it runs, what it holds, what it knows and must not know, what it passes to whom, and what survives when one part is gone; and only then was the decision (streaming, the scrollback as the only buffer) quick. The protocol's 'A design decision comes with its mechanism' asks for 'how the thing works today' but does not say that means the parts and their boundaries, nor that the failure of each part and what the existing parts already provide belong in the first message.
close_reason: Fixed by a50dcf1
